newsitem.title: USA: White House takes umbrage at Dole "Bozo" remark.
newsitem.headline: White House takes umbrage at Dole "Bozo" remark.

text.p: The White House said on Tuesday Republican Bob Dole must be getting desperate to refer to President Bill Clinton as "Bozo."
"Bozo's on his way out," Dole said in Lyndhurst, New Jersey, after a boisterous supporter reached out to shake his hand and shouted, "Please get Bozo out of the White House."
Said White House spokesman Mike McCurry: "It's not hard to imagine that Senator Dole might be feeling a little desperate at this point."

Use of the derogatory term -- Bozo is a popular television clown -- recalled then-President George Bush's remark during the 1992 campaign that his dog Millie knew more about foreign policy "than those two Bozos," referring to Clinton and his running mate Al Gore.
McCurry said he felt Dole comported himself with civility during the Clinton-Dole debate Sunday night.

"I think he gained some ground in front of the American people by being humorous, by being respectful and by conducting himself in a civil manner on Sunday night. If he chooses to conduct himself in a different fashion in the next debate, the American people can make some judgment about what they think about it," he told reporters.
He added: "I can easily understand if he wants to try a new strategy. He's got a new strategy every couple of days. Maybe he's going to take a new tack. We'll wait and see what happens."
